aiGeneration.promptName: Aardvark Consulting Process from Meeting Transcript 2 — AI prompt
aiGeneration.promptText:
Build the BPMN process from this meeting transcript. Treat each distinct speaker as a role / lane, and use roles or job functions — never an individual person's name — in pool, lane, task and annotation names. Ignore small talk.

Process: Lead qualification for the development area at Aardvark Consulting.

Roles / participants: Development Manager (process owner, also conducts discovery calls), Customer Success Manager (acts as "setter"), Principal Consultants, Microsoft (referral partner), Customer / Prospect.
Systems / data: leads inbox (email), web ads as lead source, high-level solution design and architecture document, process map.

1. Start: a lead arrives. Leads come through one of three channels, and the qualification path differs by channel.

Decision — lead channel:
   Branch A: Web lead (from web ads)
   Branch B: Microsoft channel (existing Microsoft customer referred by Microsoft)
   Branch C: Existing customer referral (new project for an existing customer)

Branch A — Web lead:
2. The lead arrives in the leads inbox.
3. The Customer Success Manager picks up the lead from the inbox.
4. The Customer Success Manager calls the prospect and runs a qualifying call: establishes what they are trying to do and works through qualifying questions covering who they are, budget authority, need and time to do it — i.e. confirming there is a real project rather than a tyre-kicker.
5. Once qualification is established, the Customer Success Manager books a discovery call with the Development Manager or one of the Principal Consultants.
6. The Development Manager or a Principal Consultant runs the discovery call with the prospect: what they are trying to do, their top two or three priorities, and their pain points.
7. Proceed to the shared co-design stage (step 12).

Branch B — Microsoft channel:
8. Microsoft introduces Aardvark Consulting to the customer, either via an introduction call or via an innovation hub workshop.
9. Aardvark Consulting holds a couple of shared meetings/workshops with Microsoft and the customer to talk through the solution.
10. Proceed to the shared co-design stage (step 12).

Branch C — Existing customer referral:
11. No introductory calls are needed (the customer is already known). A single discovery workshop is held to discover the particular use case, then proceed directly to solution design (step 12).

Shared path — Proposal co-design:
12. Run a proposal co-design workshop, or a series of workshops (one or many), with the customer: work through the problem or what is to be built, workshop the customer's process, build out a process map of the intended solution, and make design decisions including how AI will be used within it.
13. After the workshop(s), Aardvark Consulting works offline to prepare a high-level solution design and architecture.
14. Aardvark Consulting presents the high-level solution design and architecture back to the customer.
15. End of the lead qualification portion of the process.

CLARIFICATIONS (answers to open questions — incorporate these):
- Disqualified lead path: Customer Success Manager sends a polite decline and the process ends as 'Lead Not Qualified'
- Co-design stage owner: Principal Consultants
- Discovery call assignment: Always the Development Manager unless unavailable, then a Principal Consultant
- Microsoft branch owner: Development Manager with a Principal Consultant attending
- Systems involved: Leads System
- Workshop repetition & end: Co-design workshops as a looping subprocess ('Repeat Until Design Agreed'), then a single end event 'Solution Design Presented'

questions.q: Are there explicit disqualification/exit points — e.g. what happens if the qualifying call shows no budget, authority, need or timeline, or if the discovery call is unsuccessful?
Who owns and runs the proposal co-design workshops and produces the high-level solution design and architecture (Development Manager, Principal Consultants, or both)?
In the Microsoft branch, is any qualifying call or discovery call performed, or does the channel skip qualification entirely?
What determines whether one or multiple co-design workshops are needed?
What happens after the solution design and architecture is presented (e.g. formal proposal, pricing, contracting)? The transcript ends at the presentation.
Is the leads inbox used only for web leads, or also for Microsoft and existing-customer referrals?
Is any CRM or other system used to record leads and qualification outcomes?
Are there service levels or timeframes for picking up a lead, making the qualifying call, or booking the discovery call?
